scr_jobcost_editing_a_memorized_report.purpose: Changes a memorized job cost report's saved settings — typically adding newly created jobs to the monthly capex status report for a lender or owner.
scr_jobcost_editing_a_memorized_report.outcome: Standard capex reports include every active project.
scr_jobcost_editing_a_memorized_report.rootCause: Memorized reports keep the job list they were saved with. When a new renovation phase or roof job starts, it is silently missing from the lender's capex package until someone edits the definition.
scr_jobcost_editing_a_memorized_report.ifSkipped: New projects are missing from capex packages and lenders see an incomplete picture of reserve-funded work.
redFlags: Active jobs absent from the memorized capex package

scr_jobcost_running_a_memorized_report_o.purpose: Runs a memorized job cost report or chart with its saved settings, adjusting only the period — the routine way to produce monthly capex packages.
scr_jobcost_running_a_memorized_report_o.outcome: Consistent monthly capex reporting produced quickly.
scr_jobcost_running_a_memorized_report_o.rootCause: Capex reporting to owners and lenders is monthly; running from a saved definition keeps layout and scope identical so changes reflect real project progress.
scr_jobcost_running_a_memorized_report_o.ifSkipped: Capex reports are rebuilt manually each month with inconsistent scope.

scr_jobcost_scheduling_a_memorized_repor.purpose: Schedules a memorized job cost report to run automatically — for example a weekly job status report to construction managers during an active renovation program.
scr_jobcost_scheduling_a_memorized_repor.outcome: Project status delivered on schedule without manual runs.
scr_jobcost_scheduling_a_memorized_repor.rootCause: Active capital programs need frequent visibility of commitments versus budget; scheduled delivery keeps construction managers informed between month-end packages.
scr_jobcost_scheduling_a_memorized_repor.ifSkipped: Construction managers commit spend without current budget information.
redFlags: Schedules delivering to former project managers

scr_jobcost_deleting_a_memorized_report_.purpose: Deletes a memorized job cost report for a finished program or a superseded format.
scr_jobcost_deleting_a_memorized_report_.outcome: The memorized library holds only current project reports.
scr_jobcost_deleting_a_memorized_report_.rootCause: Old capex definitions for closed programs remain selectable and get run by mistake, sending outdated project lists to lenders.
scr_jobcost_deleting_a_memorized_report_.ifSkipped: Outdated capex packages reach lenders or owners.

scr_jobcost_edit_memorized_report_page.purpose: The page for changing a memorized job cost report's name, parameters, sharing and output format.
scr_jobcost_edit_memorized_report_page.outcome: Project report definitions maintained in one place.
scr_jobcost_edit_memorized_report_page.rootCause: Shared capex definitions are used by the whole team; edits here change every package produced from them and should be deliberate and communicated.
scr_jobcost_edit_memorized_report_page.ifSkipped: Definitions change without the team knowing, and packages shift unexpectedly.

scr_jobcost_schedule_memorized_report_pa.purpose: The page for setting frequency, time, recipients and format of a scheduled job cost report.
scr_jobcost_schedule_memorized_report_pa.outcome: Automated distribution of project reports to the right people.
scr_jobcost_schedule_memorized_report_pa.rootCause: Recipients and timing decide whether scheduled reports help; sending before month-end reclasses are done distributes preliminary project costs.
scr_jobcost_schedule_memorized_report_pa.ifSkipped: Preliminary figures reach lenders, or reports go to the wrong people.

scr_jobcost_job_setup_summary_report.purpose: Summarizes how jobs are set up — property, type, dates, status, manager, funding sources and budget totals — for review of the capital program's structure.
scr_jobcost_job_setup_summary_report.outcome: A check that every project is set up completely and consistently.
scr_jobcost_job_setup_summary_report.rootCause: Setup errors (missing funding source, wrong job type) make projects fall out of draws or reserve reports. A setup summary exposes them before they cause missed reimbursements.
scr_jobcost_job_setup_summary_report.ifSkipped: Setup gaps are discovered only when a draw or reserve report is wrong.

scr_jobcost_job_setup_summary_report_opt.purpose: Parameters for the Job Setup Summary report — properties, job types, status and which setup attributes to show.
scr_jobcost_job_setup_summary_report_opt.outcome: A focused setup review, for example all active reserve-funded jobs.
scr_jobcost_job_setup_summary_report_opt.rootCause: Setup reviews are usually targeted at one program or lender; options scope the report accordingly.
scr_jobcost_job_setup_summary_report_opt.ifSkipped: Reviews are unfocused and gaps go unnoticed.
redFlags: Closed jobs included in active program reviews

scr_jobcost_job_setup_summary_report_col.purpose: Explains the Job Setup Summary columns — job, property, type, status, dates, manager, funding sources and budget.
scr_jobcost_job_setup_summary_report_col.outcome: Correct reading of project setup attributes.
scr_jobcost_job_setup_summary_report_col.rootCause: Funding source and type columns determine which draws and reports a job appears in; reading them correctly reveals misconfigured jobs.
scr_jobcost_job_setup_summary_report_col.ifSkipped: Misconfigured jobs are overlooked and later drop out of draws or reserve reports.
redFlags: Reserve jobs typed as ordinary capex

scr_jobcost_job_cost_activity_report.purpose: Reports transactions posted to jobs over a period — invoices, JEs, commitments — by job and segment, with vendor and reference detail.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_activity_report.outcome: A transaction-level record of project spending for draws, audits and review.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_activity_report.rootCause: Draw packages and capital additions audits require transaction detail behind job totals; the activity report supplies it in one document.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_activity_report.ifSkipped: Draws and audits lack transaction support and are delayed.
redFlags: Operating expenses appearing on capital jobs

scr_jobcost_job_cost_activity_report_opt.purpose: Parameters for the Job Cost Activity report — jobs, segments, date range, transaction types and detail level.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_activity_report_opt.outcome: Activity scoped to exactly the draw period or audit sample.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_activity_report_opt.rootCause: Draws cover specific date ranges and jobs; matching report options to the draw prevents including costs from other periods.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_activity_report_opt.ifSkipped: Draw support includes costs from the wrong period.
redFlags: Date range not matching the draw period

scr_jobcost_job_cost_activity_report_col.purpose: Explains Job Cost Activity columns — date, source, reference, vendor, segment, amount.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_activity_report_col.rootCause: The source column distinguishes invoices from JEs; JEs on capital jobs deserve extra scrutiny because they bypass A/P approval.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_activity_report_col.ifSkipped: Manual journal entries on capital jobs escape the extra scrutiny they need.

scr_jobcost_cost_code_structure_report.purpose: Shows the cost code (segment) structure used for jobs — codes, descriptions and hierarchy.
scr_jobcost_cost_code_structure_report.outcome: A reference of cost codes for coding invoices and building budgets consistently.
scr_jobcost_cost_code_structure_report.rootCause: Consistent cost codes across projects allow comparison and lender-friendly draws; the structure report is the reference everyone codes against.
scr_jobcost_cost_code_structure_report.ifSkipped: Projects use inconsistent codes and cannot be compared.

scr_jobcost_cost_code_structure_report_o.purpose: Parameters for the Cost Code Structure report — code ranges and levels to include.
scr_jobcost_cost_code_structure_report_o.outcome: A focused view of relevant cost codes.
scr_jobcost_cost_code_structure_report_o.rootCause: Large code structures are unwieldy; filtering to the relevant range helps construction managers code correctly.
scr_jobcost_cost_code_structure_report_o.ifSkipped: Staff pick wrong codes from a long, unfiltered list.

scr_jobcost_cost_code_structure_report_c.purpose: Explains the Cost Code Structure report columns — cost code, description, level and parent code — which show how trade-level codes roll up into summary categories on job reports and draws.
scr_jobcost_cost_code_structure_report_c.outcome: Correct understanding of how codes roll up.
scr_jobcost_cost_code_structure_report_c.rootCause: Roll-up relationships determine how trade costs summarize in job reports and draws.
scr_jobcost_cost_code_structure_report_c.ifSkipped: Roll-ups are misunderstood and summaries misread.
redFlags: Codes without parents in a hierarchical structure

scr_jobcost_job_budget_report.purpose: Reports job budgets by segment — original, change orders, revised — for one or more jobs.
scr_jobcost_job_budget_report.outcome: A budget document for owner and lender review of each project.
scr_jobcost_job_budget_report.rootCause: Owners and lenders approve and monitor projects against budget; this report presents the approved budget and its changes clearly.
scr_jobcost_job_budget_report.ifSkipped: Budget presentations are assembled manually and may not match the system.
redFlags: Revised budgets without change order support

scr_jobcost_job_budget_report_options.purpose: Parameters for the Job Budget report — jobs, segments, and whether to include change order detail.
scr_jobcost_job_budget_report_options.outcome: Budget reports scoped to the review.
scr_jobcost_job_budget_report_options.rootCause: Lenders often want change order detail; owners may want totals only. Options produce the right level for each audience.
scr_jobcost_job_budget_report_options.ifSkipped: Reports show the wrong level of detail for the audience.
redFlags: Change order detail omitted for lender reports

scr_jobcost_job_budget_report_columns.purpose: Explains Job Budget report columns — segment, original budget, change orders, revised budget.
scr_jobcost_job_budget_report_columns.rootCause: Separating original and change order amounts shows how much the project has grown, a key lender metric.
scr_jobcost_job_budget_report_columns.ifSkipped: Budget growth is misread and lenders are given the wrong picture of project scope changes.

scr_jobcost_job_cost_draw_detail_report.purpose: Details a job cost draw — each invoice included, vendor, amount, funding source allocation and supporting documents — as the package submitted to a construction lender or equity partner.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_draw_detail_report.outcome: A complete, lender-ready draw request supported by transaction detail.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_draw_detail_report.rootCause: Construction lenders fund only against documented, eligible costs. The draw detail report is the standard evidence package they review before releasing funds.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_draw_detail_report.ifSkipped: Draws are rejected or delayed, and the project runs short of funding.
redFlags: Costs already included in prior draws

scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.purpose: Selects the draw, detail level and attachments and runs the Job Cost Draw Detail report.
scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.outcome: A draw package produced in the lender's required format.
scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.rootCause: Each lender has its own package expectations; parameters let the accountant match them without manual rework.
scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.ifSkipped: Draw packages do not meet lender requirements and are returned.

scr_jobcost_job_cost_draw_detail_report_.purpose: Explains the Job Cost Draw Detail columns — invoice, vendor, date, amount, segment, funding allocation.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_draw_detail_report_.outcome: Correct reading of what a draw contains.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_draw_detail_report_.rootCause: Funding allocation columns show each source's share; lenders check that they are funding only their portion.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_draw_detail_report_.ifSkipped: Allocation errors in draws go unnoticed until the lender rejects them.

scr_jobcost_replacement_reserves_draw_de.purpose: Details a replacement reserve draw — qualifying invoices, proof of payment, amounts — as the reimbursement request to the loan servicer.
scr_jobcost_replacement_reserves_draw_de.rootCause: Servicers reimburse only documented, paid, eligible repairs. This report is the standard package they review; incomplete packages are rejected.
scr_jobcost_replacement_reserves_draw_de.ifSkipped: Reserve reimbursements are delayed or rejected and the property funds capital work from operating cash.

scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.purpose: Selects the reserve draw, detail and attachments and runs the Replacement Reserves Draw Detail report.
scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.outcome: A reserve draw package in the servicer's expected format.
scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.rootCause: Servicers (Fannie Mae DUS lenders, Freddie Mac servicers) have specific package requirements; parameters produce compliant packages.
scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.ifSkipped: Packages are returned for missing items.

scr_jobcost_replacement_reserves_draw_de.purpose: Explains the reserve draw detail columns — invoice, vendor, paid date, check number, amount.
scr_jobcost_replacement_reserves_draw_de.outcome: Correct reading of reserve draw contents.
scr_jobcost_replacement_reserves_draw_de.rootCause: Paid date and check number columns prove payment, which servicers require before reimbursing.
scr_jobcost_replacement_reserves_draw_de.ifSkipped: Unpaid items slip into reimbursement requests.

scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_report.purpose: Reports each job's financial status by segment — revised budget, commitments, cost to date, remaining budget and percent spent — as the standard monthly capex status report.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_report.outcome: A monthly capex status package for owners and lenders.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_report.rootCause: Owners and lenders monitor capital programs monthly; this report is the canonical view of budget versus committed versus spent.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_report.ifSkipped: Capex monitoring relies on ad hoc spreadsheets and overruns are reported late.
redFlags: Negative remaining budget on any segment

scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_report_optio.purpose: Parameters for the Job Cost Status report — jobs, as-of date, segments and whether commitments are included.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_report_optio.outcome: Status reports scoped to the audience and period.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_report_optio.rootCause: Excluding commitments makes projects look healthier than they are; options must be set to show the true position.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_report_optio.ifSkipped: Status reports exclude commitments and overstate remaining budget.

scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_report_colum.purpose: Explains Job Cost Status columns — revised budget, pending and approved commitments, cost to date, remaining and percent complete.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_report_colum.outcome: Correct interpretation of project financial health.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_report_colum.rootCause: Remaining budget should subtract commitments, not just costs; readers must understand which columns are included.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_report_colum.ifSkipped: Remaining budget is misread as larger than it is.
redFlags: Percent spent far ahead of physical progress

scr_jobcost_job_status_summary_report.purpose: Summarizes job status at job level (not segment) across the portfolio — budget, committed, spent, remaining.
scr_jobcost_job_status_summary_report.outcome: A one-line-per-project summary for executive and owner review.
scr_jobcost_job_status_summary_report.rootCause: Executives and asset managers want a portfolio view of capital programs before drilling into trades.
scr_jobcost_job_status_summary_report.ifSkipped: Portfolio capex status is compiled manually.
redFlags: Jobs with spend but no recent activity (stalled)

scr_jobcost_job_status_summary_report_op.purpose: Parameters for the Job Status Summary report — properties, job types, status and as-of date.
scr_jobcost_job_status_summary_report_op.outcome: Portfolio summaries scoped to the program or owner.
scr_jobcost_job_status_summary_report_op.rootCause: Different owners want summaries of their own programs only; options enforce that scope.
scr_jobcost_job_status_summary_report_op.ifSkipped: Portfolio summaries mix different owners' capital projects.

scr_jobcost_job_status_summary_report_co.purpose: Explains Job Status Summary columns — job, budget, committed, cost to date, remaining.
scr_jobcost_job_status_summary_report_co.outcome: Correct reading of the portfolio summary.
scr_jobcost_job_status_summary_report_co.rootCause: Understanding that committed amounts are included in the remaining calculation prevents overstating available budget.
scr_jobcost_job_status_summary_report_co.ifSkipped: Available budget is overstated in executive reviews.

scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_by_month_rep.purpose: Shows job costs by month against the monthly budget curve — the actual spending pattern versus plan.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_by_month_rep.outcome: Visibility of whether projects are spending ahead of or behind schedule.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_by_month_rep.rootCause: Funding (draws, capital calls) is planned by month; comparing actual monthly spend to plan shows when funding needs will shift.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_by_month_rep.ifSkipped: Funding needs are mistimed and draws or capital calls come late.
reports: Job Cost Status by Month report
redFlags: Spend far ahead of the planned curve

scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_by_month_rep.purpose: Parameters for the Job Cost Status by Month report — jobs, months and comparison basis.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_by_month_rep.outcome: Monthly spend reports scoped to the funding review.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_by_month_rep.rootCause: Funding reviews cover specific months and jobs; options produce the needed window.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_by_month_rep.ifSkipped: Funding reviews use incomplete month windows and mistime draws.
reports: Job Cost Status by Month report
redFlags: Months outside the project period included

scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_by_month_rep.purpose: Explains monthly status columns — month, budget, actual, variance and cumulative.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_by_month_rep.outcome: Correct reading of spend timing versus plan.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_by_month_rep.rootCause: Cumulative columns show whether early overspending is a timing issue or a true overrun.
scr_jobcost_job_cost_status_by_month_rep.ifSkipped: Timing differences are mistaken for overruns or vice versa.
reports: Job Cost Status by Month report

scr_jobcost_wip_account_reconciliation_r.purpose: Reconciles the work-in-progress (Construction in Progress) GL balance to the sum of open job costs, identifying differences between the GL and job subledger.
scr_jobcost_wip_account_reconciliation_r.outcome: A monthly tie-out proving the CIP balance on the balance sheet is supported by open projects.
scr_jobcost_wip_account_reconciliation_r.rootCause: CIP is often touched by entries outside Job Cost (JEs without job coding, capitalizations to fixed assets). Without a reconciliation, CIP carries unexplained balances or completed projects never leave CIP.
scr_jobcost_wip_account_reconciliation_r.ifSkipped: CIP carries unsupported balances, completed projects are not capitalized, and auditors flag the account.

scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.purpose: Selects properties, as-of date and WIP accounts and runs the WIP reconciliation.
scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.outcome: A CIP tie-out for the period end.
scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.rootCause: The as-of date must match the balance sheet date and include every CIP account for the tie-out to be meaningful.
scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.ifSkipped: False differences are reported or real ones missed.
redFlags: As-of date not equal to month-end

scr_jobcost_wip_account_reconciliation_r.purpose: Explains WIP reconciliation columns — GL balance, job cost balance and difference by account or job.
scr_jobcost_wip_account_reconciliation_r.outcome: Differences traced to specific jobs or entries.
scr_jobcost_wip_account_reconciliation_r.rootCause: Knowing whether the difference sits in a specific job or in un-coded GL activity directs the fix.
scr_jobcost_wip_account_reconciliation_r.ifSkipped: Differences are hard to trace and persist.
redFlags: Differences from JEs without job coding

scr_jobcost_open_invoices_report.purpose: Lists unpaid invoices coded to jobs — amounts owed to contractors and suppliers on capital projects.
scr_jobcost_open_invoices_report.outcome: Visibility of project payables due, for payment planning and draw timing.
scr_jobcost_open_invoices_report.rootCause: Contractor payment timing affects lien risk and draw eligibility (many reserve draws require paid invoices). Open job invoices must be managed separately from routine A/P.
scr_jobcost_open_invoices_report.ifSkipped: Contractors are paid late (lien risk) and draws are delayed awaiting payment.
redFlags: Contractor invoices older than prompt-pay deadlines

scr_jobcost_open_invoices_report_options.purpose: Parameters for the Open Invoices report — jobs, vendors, aging buckets and as-of date — used to list unpaid contractor and supplier invoices on capital projects.
scr_jobcost_open_invoices_report_options.outcome: A focused list of unpaid project invoices.
scr_jobcost_open_invoices_report_options.rootCause: Payment planning and draw preparation need open invoices for specific jobs and dates.

scr_jobcost_open_invoices_report_columns.purpose: Explains Open Invoices columns — vendor, invoice, date, due date, amount, retainage.
scr_jobcost_open_invoices_report_columns.rootCause: Showing retainage separately from the current amount due prevents the payment team from releasing retainage with the regular payment run before the contractor's work is complete and accepted.
scr_jobcost_open_invoices_report_columns.ifSkipped: Retainage is paid before completion and the owner loses leverage over punch-list work.
redFlags: Retainage included in current payment runs

scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.purpose: Selects jobs, vendors and the as-of date and runs the Retainage Register, producing the schedule of retainage held that supports 2015 Retainage Payable at period end.
scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.outcome: A retainage schedule for the period end.
scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.rootCause: Retainage must be tied to 2015 Retainage Payable at period end; the as-of date and scope must match the balance sheet.
scr_jobcost_customizing_and_running_the_.ifSkipped: Retainage schedules do not tie to the balance sheet.

scr_jobcost_retainage_register_report_co.purpose: Explains Retainage Register columns — invoice, vendor, retainage withheld, retainage paid and balance.
scr_jobcost_retainage_register_report_co.rootCause: Balance columns identify retainage due for release at completion and prevent duplicate release.
scr_jobcost_retainage_register_report_co.ifSkipped: Retainage is released twice or not at all.

scr_jobcost_job_information_page.purpose: The job record page with tabs for general information, budgets, units, funding sources and settings.
scr_jobcost_job_information_page.outcome: A complete definition of the capital project.
scr_jobcost_job_information_page.rootCause: Every tab affects how the job behaves in draws, reserves and reports; incomplete records cause projects to drop out of those processes.
scr_jobcost_job_information_page.ifSkipped: Projects are missing from draws or reports because setup is incomplete.

scr_jobcost_recalculating_job_totals.purpose: Recalculates a job's totals (budget, commitments, costs) after changes or data corrections.
scr_jobcost_recalculating_job_totals.outcome: Job totals reflect all current transactions.
scr_jobcost_recalculating_job_totals.rootCause: Imports, reclasses and interface corrections can leave cached totals stale; recalculating refreshes them.
scr_jobcost_recalculating_job_totals.ifSkipped: Job status shows stale totals and capex reports disagree with the underlying transactions.

scr_jobcost_transferring_a_job_to_anothe.purpose: Moves a job and its activity to another property — for example when a project was set up under the wrong property or a campus is split into separate entities.
scr_jobcost_transferring_a_job_to_anothe.outcome: Project costs sit on the correct property and owner.
scr_jobcost_transferring_a_job_to_anothe.rootCause: Capital costs belong to the property that owns the improvement; a job under the wrong property misstates both properties' fixed assets and draws.
scr_jobcost_transferring_a_job_to_anothe.ifSkipped: Fixed assets and reserve draws are recorded at the wrong property.
redFlags: Transfers between different owners without approval

scr_jobcost_reopening_a_jobs_closed_cost.purpose: Reopens cost codes that were closed on a job so legitimate late costs (a final invoice, warranty work) can post.
scr_jobcost_reopening_a_jobs_closed_cost.outcome: Valid late costs recorded on the right trade.
scr_jobcost_reopening_a_jobs_closed_cost.rootCause: Final invoices sometimes arrive after a trade is closed; reopening avoids coding them to wrong codes.
scr_jobcost_reopening_a_jobs_closed_cost.ifSkipped: Legitimate late costs are coded to the wrong trade because the right one is closed.
redFlags: Codes reopened after capitalization without adjusting the asset

scr_jobcost_adding_units_to_a_job.purpose: Associates specific units with a job — for example the 40 units renovated in Phase 2 — so costs can be analyzed per unit.
scr_jobcost_adding_units_to_a_job.outcome: Renovation cost per unit and rent premium analysis by unit.
scr_jobcost_adding_units_to_a_job.rootCause: Value-add programs are judged by cost per unit and the rent premium achieved; linking units to jobs enables that return-on-cost analysis.
scr_jobcost_adding_units_to_a_job.ifSkipped: Cost per unit and renovation ROI cannot be calculated from the system.
